generalized_learning.generalized_failure_pattern: A verification pipeline can label evidence as exact-subject while actually executing tests on an implicit synthetic or merge checkout, making the certificate stronger than the execution that produced it.
generalized_learning.plausible_wrong_implementation: A workflow records the intended subject identifier in a manifest but leaves checkout selection implicit, so tests execute a different revision while the manifest still looks internally consistent.
trigger_signals: verification manifest declares a subject identifier
checkout action has no explicit subject ref
provider event uses a synthetic integration revision
generalized_learning.reusable_control: Before accepting exact-subject evidence, compare the revision physically checked out by the verification job with the revision declared as the evidence subject and fail closed on any mismatch.
generalized_learning.prevention_rule: Verification jobs that issue exact-subject claims must explicitly check out the declared subject before executing measurements or tests; synthetic integration checks remain separate evidence.
generalized_learning.detection_rule: The evidence manifest must record both declared subject and observed checkout identifiers, and a gate must reject publication unless they are equal for exact-subject evidence.

transfer_cases.scenario: Synthetic integration event differs from declared verification subject; explicit checkout is required before tests.
Manifest carries distinct declared and observed revisions; exact-subject certification rejects the mismatch.

skill_changes.evidence: The verification job explicitly checks out the declared subject before exact-head TypeScript/tests and keeps merge-preview integration in a separate job.
The repository CI contract check enforces the exact-head verification structure and the successful run emitted matching headSha/checkoutSha.
